## DuckDB

Point `rush` at a [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) database (`.duckdb` or `.ddb`)
and every table is read into the `dfs` list, keyed by table name:

```{bash}
rush run 'names(dfs$shop)' shop.duckdb
```

If a database holds a single table, it is also bound to `df` for convenience,
so a one-table database behaves just like any other single input.

### Writing to DuckDB

Write to DuckDB with `-o output.duckdb`. When the result is a named list (e.g.
from multiple inputs), each element becomes a separate table:

```{bash}
echo "id,val
1,a
2,b" > a.csv
echo "id,val
3,c
4,d" > b.csv
rush convert -o combined.duckdb a.csv b.csv
rush run 'names(dfs$combined)' combined.duckdb
```

A single file uses the file stem as the table name:

```{bash}
rush convert -o penguins_db.duckdb penguins.csv
rush sql "SELECT species, COUNT(*) AS n FROM penguins_db.penguins GROUP BY species" penguins_db.duckdb
rm -f penguins_db.duckdb
```

### Querying with SQL

A `.duckdb` file is attached as a schema, and its tables are accessible as
`schema.table`:

```{bash}
rush sql "SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total
          FROM shop.customers c JOIN shop.orders o ON c.id = o.cust
          GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY total DESC" shop.duckdb
```

## SQLite

Files ending in `.sqlite` or `.db` are read with
[RSQLite](https://rsqlite.r-dbi.org/). All tables are loaded into the `dfs`
list, similar to DuckDB:

```{bash}
rush convert -o app.sqlite penguins.csv
rush run 'names(dfs$app)' app.sqlite
rm -f app.sqlite
```

### Writing to SQLite

Like DuckDB, multiple inputs become separate tables:

```{bash}
rush convert -o combined.sqlite a.csv b.csv
rush run 'names(dfs$combined)' combined.sqlite
```

### Converting between database formats

Copy all tables from one database to another:

```{bash}
rush convert -o copy.sqlite shop.duckdb
rush run 'names(dfs$copy)' copy.sqlite
```

```{bash}
#| include: false
rm -f a.csv b.csv combined.duckdb combined.sqlite copy.sqlite
```
